title: He passed the toughest exam of the British Raj - then got dismissed on a technicality. It made him a founder of Indian politics.
caption:
He passed the toughest exam of the British Raj - then got dismissed on a technicality. It made him a founder of Indian politics.

He passed the Indian Civil Service exam in 1869 - one of the first Indians to do so - but was dismissed in 1874 on a technicality, an injustice that pushed him from the civil service into public life.

He led it into merging with the Indian National Congress in 1886, presided over Congress in 1895 and became a leading voice against the 1905 Partition of Bengal and the Swadeshi movement that followed - earning him the title 'Rashtraguru,' Teacher of the Nation.

Banerjee's dismissal could have ended his public life before it started. Instead, it became the reason Indian political organizing took its first organized shape.
